content: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Enforcement Division. This is Officer Michael Grant, badge number 521-104. With whom am I speaking?
Hi, um, this is Emily Carter. I got a call that said my business was out of compliance? I'm not sure what this is about.

Ms. Carter, this call pertains to your recent federal tax filings. According to IRS records, you have failed to submit required payroll tax documents and 1099 forms for your freelance business for the past fiscal year.
I, I thought I filed everything. I just started working for myself last year and used an online tax service. What did I miss?

Let me be clear, Ms. Carter. Failure to properly report and remit payroll taxes is a direct violation of Internal Revenue Code Section 7201. This is a serious compliance breach. Are you aware that such infractions can result in substantial penalties and federal audit proceedings?
No, I didn't know. I've never been in trouble before. What's going to happen to me?

At this stage, your case has triggered a provisional asset freeze and your business license is at risk of immediate suspension. Unless you resolve this today, the IRS will escalate to full asset seizure and initiate collections through the Department of Justice.
Wait, what? You're going to freeze my bank accounts? I just got started, I can't lose everything.

Ms. Carter, it is my duty to inform you: non-compliance on federal tax obligations is a criminal offense. If you do not act now, you may face a minimum $9,200 penalty and irreversible damage to your credit. There's also the possibility of a federal warrant being issued in your name.
This is terrifying. I have so much student debt, I can't afford any more trouble. Please, is there anything I can do to fix this?

I can offer you a pre-litigation settlement if you comply with our instructions immediately. The IRS allows a one-time opportunity to resolve such matters outside of court by submitting the required payment today.
What kind of payment? I don't understand what I'm supposed to do.

You are to remit an urgent compliance bond of $2,500 as a demonstration of good faith. This must be delivered via federally approved payment methods only, either a direct wire to the IRS settlement account or by providing the codes from government-authorized prepaid cards such as Apple or Google Play.
Prepaid cards? Isn't that a little strange? I thought payments to the IRS were different.

Ms. Carter, these procedures are standard for expedited compliance settlements as outlined in IRS Bulletin 4212-B. Do not question federal protocol. If you fail to comply, your file will be transferred to enforcement and your assets seized without further notice.
Okay, okay, I'm sorry, I just don't have $2,500 right now. What am I supposed to do?

How much liquid funds do you have access to at this moment, either in your bank account or available credit? The settlement must be paid in full, but partial payment may delay enforcement by 24 hours.
I have maybe $800 on my card. That's all.

Then you must proceed to your nearest retail location and purchase $800 worth of Apple gift cards. Remain on this call while you do so. Once acquired, read the codes on the back to me for immediate processing.
You want me to go right now? On the phone? I have to go buy gift cards?
Correct. Do not disconnect this call. If you hang up or delay, your tax delinquency will be escalated to the federal collections unit. Is that understood?
Yes, I understand. I'm just really scared.
Stay calm and follow my instructions. Once you have the gift cards, return to your car and read the codes to me. This is the only way to halt further action today.
